name: Unlimited Third-Party Indemnification
description: Provider is required to indemnify the customer for any third-party claims without any financial cap.
why_it_matters: One large lawsuit could bankrupt the company if there is no limit on indemnity obligations.
plain_english: We pay for all legal costs if someone sues you, no matter how much it costs.
how_it_should_be: Indemnity should be capped at a reasonable multiple of fees paid (e.g., 2x or 3x).
negotiation_script: We need to align our risk with the value of the contract. Let's cap this at 2x annual fees.
suggested_alternative: Provider's total liability under this section shall not exceed 200% of the total fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim.

name: Ambiguous Data Ownership
description: The contract does not explicitly state that the Customer owns their input data.
why_it_matters: If you don't own your data, the provider might claim rights to it or prevent you from moving to another service.
plain_english: It's not clear who owns the information you upload to the system.
how_it_should_be: Customer should explicitly own all 'Customer Data'.
negotiation_script: We must ensure we retain full ownership of our proprietary data uploaded to your platform.
suggested_alternative: As between the parties, Customer owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Customer Data.

name: Unlimited CAM Expense Pass-Through
description: Landlord can pass through any Common Area Maintenance (CAM) costs without a cap on year-over-year increases.
why_it_matters: Operating expenses can skyrocket unexpectedly, making the lease unaffordable.
plain_english: The landlord can charge you extra for building repairs whenever they want.
how_it_should_be: CAM increases should be capped (e.g., 5% per year).
negotiation_script: We need budget predictability. Can we cap the controllable CAM increases at 5% annually?
suggested_alternative: Controllable Operating Expenses shall not increase by more than 5% over the amount for the immediately preceding calendar year.

name: Overly Broad Non-Compete
description: Prevents the employee from working for any competitor in any capacity for 2 years globally.
why_it_matters: This can effectively prevent an employee from finding a new job in their field.
plain_english: You can't work for any similar company anywhere in the world for two years after you leave.
how_it_should_be: Non-competes should be limited in time (e.g., 6 months) and geography.
negotiation_script: This scope is too broad. Can we limit this to direct competitors within 50 miles for 6 months?
suggested_alternative: Employee shall not work for a Direct Competitor in the Greater London area for a period of 6 months following termination.
